chapter: Brass bands, Eddie Miller and band stories
title: The Invincibles, Doc Souchon and New Orleans versus Chicago jazz
summary: Brownlee refers the Invincibles' instrumentation to Dr. Souchon, and recalls his This Is Your Life appearance and Eddie Condon's quip about New Orleans and Chicago jazz.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I didn't get the Invincibles instruments. Who played what in that?

Well, there was about 16 altogether. Of course, they wouldn't have that many all the time, but we'd go around and play parties. I would suggest you ask Dr. Suchon about that. I think Dr. could tell you about it. I think he'd remember it. But when I saw Dr. Suchon on This Is Your Life, did you see that?
Well, do you remember the fellow Billy Kleppinger?
You remember when he said, Billy, you lead, did you take it off? And Billy went in and playing the mandolin.

Well, I thought sure that Billy was going to go into ragging scales. And he had Red Mackie on bass that night, too. and Sushant on, well they had quite an aggregation there that night and there was one little thing in there that of course the boys in Chicago and the boys in New Orleans always got along fine and they did have a beat, a similar beat, but somebody, Eddie Condon it was, they said what's the difference between New Orleans jazz and Chicago jazz and Eddie said a thousand miles. Well it's a little few miles more than a thousand and aside from that there is a little faint difference. I got it. But that was a very fine remark, very fine gesture on his part and it was well received by me because a lot of the boys in Chicago and the boys in New Orleans have always gotten along wonderfully well, fine, just fine. And you can always find that out at the Blue Note, you go around the Blue Note you can always find some Chicago boys there. And pretty near run into some New Orleans boys mixed up with them.
